scope: Current core/Messaging/Signal-provider runtime boundary, store outcome and mention parser checks, and source profiles with and without optional AI. Full nine-provider conformance remains pending.
notes: Valid maximum-size local posts now use runtime-owned result references. An interim version rejected local size expansion; it is not the final behavior.
The private runtime owner uses existing state and adds no fake provider adapter or new process tree. Public references contain no PID, table, raw bytes, or lazy stream.
Core resource lookup clears expired/dead-call values on access. Active values retain creator-process ownership.
Compiler clause grouping warnings were fixed. The stale dependency PLT was refreshed; final Dialyzer reports zero errors, skips, and unused ignores.

The combined-directory test attempt failed on seven relative story fixture paths and showed duplicate test module warnings. Stable fixture paths and separate complete suite processes pass; the original failed log is retained.
The runtime graph profile is G3 evidence. It does not replace all nine adapter ports, G7 whole-group conformance, the 90 percent coverage floor, PRs, or current-head CI.
Current acceptance tests prove safe storage errors and partial-unit retry ownership. G4 mapper checks do not replace full Telegram normalizer, webhook/polling, operation, or checkpoint conformance.

Message-store error, raise, throw, exit and invalid return cases distinguish confirmed absence, confirmed write and uncertain read. Repeated acceptance has one write after a confirmed or uncertain outcome. Unknown claims are held until explicit clearing or runtime shutdown, and have no restart guarantee.

A stopped room supervisor after the write keeps the accepted message and emits a registered observation failure. Lifecycle update exceptions before or after writes return safe errors; retry does not repeat a confirmed update.

Fourteen private mention-parser tests cover helper arities, exception fallbacks, text limits, malformed metadata, command selection and Unicode spans. A span that cuts a Unicode code point no longer crashes or removes text. Normalizer coverage is 90.2 percent; package coverage is 78.9 percent.

The first full message-outcome run exposed an incomplete old test store with no confirmation read. Add the real ETS read and preserve its original retry assertions. Initial failure logs remain in this bundle.
Refresh the actual Telegram/Slack runtime fixtures after the Messaging change: 7 Slack membership, 4 Slack execution/selection, and 8 Telegram membership cases pass in the pinned pair profile.

Ten lifecycle delete failure cases preserve safe errors, parent identity and exact delete counts. A retry cannot repeat an already completed delete. Stopped runtime and deduper cases return safe contract errors before any store/provider call.

Private ingress subscription metadata stays in caller bridge/adapter scope for map/struct responses and all four page wrappers. Malformed page records or wrappers fail before metadata writes. Deletion preserves foreign bridge records.
Nine dead-letter record tests prove capacity/order, archive/purge ownership, replay admission/cache/force rules, failure retry and missing/unavailable state without executing a provider operation.

Twelve provider-free CLI cases cover runtime-only startup, dotenv/system variables, CLI/YAML bridge routes, missing credentials/IDs/modules and invalid files/topology. Echo needs no provider credential. Correct Dotenvy defaults and the typed source/2 call preserve environment precedence. A failed topology stops its newly started supervisor.

Current inclusive checks pass 1050 checks in each pinned runtime profile, including local PostgreSQL. Harness 241 per profile and optional AI 4 pass. Package quality has zero Dialyzer errors/skips; compiled audit has 5031 exports including 1200 generated instance exports. Coverage is 80.5 percent, still below 90 percent.
